newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Indians protest gold mining project.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Indians protest gold mining project.

text.p: Indian leaders from Venezuela's remote southeastern region travelled to the capital on Thursday to protest against a controversial plan to turn a huge tropical forest reserve into a gold mining project.

Dressed in city clothes but wearing straw headbands lightly decorated with white beads and red feathers, about 80 native chiefs urged congressmen to oppose the government's scheme to develop the Imataca reserve, near the Guayanese border.
"Mining at a world level is a destroyer," said Jerrick Aaedn, a Pemon Indian leader from southeastern Bolivar state.
Government officials argue the delicate ecosystem is already being destroyed by about 20,000 illegal miners from neighbouring countries working gold reserves valued at $150 billion.
The government proposes to open Imataca to more orderly and controlled mining by large foreign companies.
"We are against mining, whether it is legal or illegal," said Indian leader Juvencio Gomez.
The Indian chief said opening up the reserve to foreign multinationals would be a deathknell for their communities already suffering insufficient education and health resources.
Ministers say deforestation has already become a problem in the forest, as has poisoining from mercury, disease and prostitution in improvised mining settlements.
